title: My Mom Went Back To School

sentences.text: Hi, my name is Zoe, and my best friend is my mom, Vicki.
She was a single mom who had me when she was really young, so people always said we looked more like sisters than mother and daughter.
Once, when I was in eighth grade, we went to a parent-teacher meeting at my school, and somehow we both ended up crushing on the same family.
I liked this cute boy in my class, and mom liked his dad.
Is there anything on my teeth?
No, Mom, you're good.
What about mine?
Perfect, just like your mama.
Then, during a snack break, Mom suddenly pretended to trip and spill our water all over my crush's dad, Mr. Tucker.
He immediately leaned in and helped her up.
Oh, thank you.
It's so hard to find a gentleman these days.
Mr. Tucker smiled politely, and Mom shot me a look like, "Your turn."
So, I walked over to my crush, tried to copy her move, and spilled my cup on him.
Except, I didn't realize I wasn't holding water.
I was holding coffee.
Very hot coffee.
He screamed and started jumping around in pain.
Oh my god, I'm so, so sorry.
Everyone rushed over to help him, and his dad looked horrified.
Mom just shook her head at me like I had failed her personally.
Then, she leaned in close and whispered, "Pass out."
What? Pass out so I can tell them you fainted because you couldn't handle causing him this much pain.
And just then, she shoved me to the floor.
See, Mr. Tucker, uh my daughter couldn't take the guilt of hurting your son, so she But Mr.
Tucker wasn't listening.
He was too busy rushing his son out of the room, and then they both tripped over me.
My crush fell on top of his already burned foot and screamed even louder.
I shot up from the floor, completely startled. Mr.
Tucker, we can still work this out. Mr.
Tucker backed away, polite, but firm.
Please, ma'am, you and your daughter need to stay away from us.
That was basically my life with Mom.
Every day It like an adventure.
Mom was loud, fearless, and always trying to make me more outgoing.
While I was shy enough to apologize when someone else stepped on my foot.
Except, our adventure mostly happened in Grandma's house because we lived with her.
And Grandma never missed a chance to remind Mom what a disappointment she was.
If you can't get a proper job, then at least make yourself useful and fix what you ruined in high school.
It's the only way to save this family.
Grandma said things like that all the time, but I never understood what she meant.
And whenever I asked Mom, she brushed it off.
Oh, your grandma is just old.
She still believes in bad luck and curses and all that spooky nonsense.
She's only 67.
Also, what bad luck? 67.
Like 67.
Then one day, Grandma got really sick and had to be rushed to the hospital.
Her face looked pale and her hands were shaking.
And the doctors kept using serious words.
One doctor handed me her medical summary and at the bottom it said, "Your grandma will only get better if you like and subscribe to MSA."
Just kidding, guys.
I wish it said that, but liking, commenting, and helping this video go viral would definitely make us feel better.
Anyway, a few days later, the hospital bills started piling up and we didn't have enough money to pay for all of it.
Mom tried everything from selling her bags to flirting with the accountant, but nothing worked.
Vicky, honey, please go back to high school and fix this if you want me to survive.
Sorry. Go back where? Mom, don't.
She deserves a normal life. Normal?
Vicky, you had a baby at 17, live in your mother's house, and once winked at a judge during your own hearing.
He added two extra charges, and I had to sell my gold bracelet to bail you out.
What is she talking about, Ma? Fine.
Our family is a a little different.
We came from a line of witches.
For a second, nobody spoke.
Okay, cool. And I'm guessing Dad is a vampire and my math teacher is a goblin.
Mom looked away.
Wait, is my math teacher a goblin?
No, just ugly.
Mom tried to explain, but I was too shocked to understand.
20 minutes later, I finally decided to listen.
According to Grandma, every woman in our family had to face a special ritual at 16 inside her own school hallway.
Same age, same time.
And because Mom missed it, the magic never passed to her.
Grandma said it stayed trapped inside her body instead, getting heavier every year until it started making her sick.
I looked at Mom, and suddenly I noticed how pale she looked.
Even the skin under her eyes had a weird pinkish tint.
Maybe Grandma wasn't being dramatic after all.
How do you miss becoming a witch, Ma?
By sneaking out to a party with a boy named Brandon who wore sunglasses indoors.
He had sensitive eyes.
I stared at Mom, and she just shrugged her shoulders mumbling, "I'm sorry."
And just like that, Mom called her shady ex-boyfriend to help.
Two days later, Mom had a brand new identity.
Her name was Violet now, which was convenient because we could still call her V.
According to her fake file, Violet was an orphan who had been raised in a very strict orphanage.
And just like that, my mom became a sophomore in my high school, and my life changed forever.
I I sitting in class when the principal came in dragging Mom behind him.
Who called this sweet little girl a stupid orphan?
Is this how we welcome a new student?
What in the world now?
I'm sure no one said that, Mr. McDonut.
She probably just misunderstood.
She can sit next to me.
Come on, Mom.
Mom suddenly shot her head up and squinted at me.
Um, are you constipated or something?
Wait a second, it's her.
Mr. McDonut, she's the bully.
My jaw literally dropped. Mr.
McDonut shook his head in disappointment.
Zoe Butterman, how could you?
I never expected this from you.
Your mother raised you better.
Mom's face immediately lit up.
You know what?
I forgive her.
At the orphanage, they taught us to forgive identity thieves and bullies.
Zoe, we're good.
What? Mr. McDonut touched his chest emotionally and asked for the class to clap for her.
Then she hopped over and sat right next to me.
I gave her a look and she whispered back.
I barged into his office without knocking, so I had to make up a story on my feet to make him feel sorry for me.
So, you throw me under the bus?
Did you know he's bald?
That's a wig he's wearing.
His poor wife has to look at that thing every morning.
And just like that, Mom became one of us.
She adjusted so fast that she made friends on the very first day.
Kids were waving at her in the hallway and even calling her Cool V.
But she just couldn't control herself.
A week later, when she saw the PE teacher, she almost started drooling.
She winked at him during basketball practice, even though I tried to stop her many times.
Then she literally blew him a kiss while throwing the ball at him.
Oops, sorry, sir.
That was when he finally had enough and reported her to the principal.
I went with her for moral support.
Big mistake. You know, Mr.
McDonut, being raised in an orphanage with no mother figure in my life, I just don't always know how to do the right thing. I'm sorry.
Mr. McDonut felt sorry for her immediately and handed her some tissues.
Then Mom opened her bag, pulled out a bottle of hair growth serum, and handed it to him.
She nodded at him like, "I got you."
It worked on my cousin.
Her name was also Zoe.
She used to have only three hairs, and now She looked at me, then continued.
Uh not bad.
Yeah, Mom used it once.
Now she has hair in places science can't explain.
Poor thing. Well, thank you, V.
I'll let this slide this time.
And for the record, I'm praying this works because let me tell you, these wigs are itchy as heck.
Now, dismissed. Chop chop.
Mom saluted him and dragged me out.
On our way to the schoolyard for break, Mom put her arm around me.
You know, Zoe, I noticed you don't have many friends.
Maybe because your face isn't very friend-worthy, honey.
But I'm going to fix that.
I'm going to make you popular, just like me.
I had no idea what that even meant.
But just then, I saw Miles coming.
He was so cute and nerdy-looking.
Exactly my type.
Of course, he had no idea I existed.
So, when he got closer, I hid behind Mom, who noticed immediately.
Please don't tell me that's your crush.
I was just starting to have hope for your social life.
Just keep walking, Mom.
Don't let him notice me.
Relax. I'll help you win him over.
But just as he reached us, he tripped on something and fell flat on his face.
Mom nudged me to help him up, but I froze.
So, she went over and helped him herself.
Wow, you look Tired and old.
This is Zoe. She's awesome. H- hi.
Hi. So, what's your name again? It's Zoe.
No, not you.
I mean her.
Oh my god, was he seriously trying to hit on Mom while ignoring me?
Then he pulled out his small notebook and started writing.
Sorry, I have this short-term memory issue, so I write down important things before I forget them.
So, your name?
The girl with the ponytail.
And he literally wrote down Mom's name and ignored mine.
When he left, Mom turned to me.
Don't worry, he's not my type.
That's not what I'm worried about.
I mean, I had never really tried to make Miles notice me before, but now I had to act fast before he started liking Mom too much.
So, a couple of days later, Mom suggested giving me a makeover.
And somehow, I became her copy.
We literally looked like twins.
And everyone started to like me, too.
We got invited to parties, study groups, and all that.
But all I wanted was for Miles to like me.
The problem was, every time Mom tried to shut him down, he took it as useful information.
I don't like guys with glasses.
He wrote that down in his notebook.
And the next time I saw him, he wasn't wearing his glasses.
I only like blond guys.
The next day, he came to school with his hair dyed blond.
I just don't like your face, all right?
Leave me alone, dude.
Then she walked away while Miles whispered to himself, That's strange.
I didn't write that down.
So, I immediately snatched his notebook.
Let me write it for you.
I wrote it down and shoved the notebook into his chest.
By the next week, he was trying to talk to Mom again.
Someone wrote in my notebook that you're a witch.
It's not my handwriting.
People have tried to prank me before, but I know better.
Oh, sweet mother of Jesus.
After that, Mom had to wear a card around her neck.
Whenever Miles came near her, she'd flip it over for him to read.
Dear Miles, no.
So, one day during lunch, while we were sitting with the coolest girls in school, I asked Mom for something.
Mom, I have a serious idea.
What? You want to become more outgoing and cool like your mama?
I said a serious idea, not science fiction.
Anyway, once you become a witch, the first thing you owe me is making Miles hate you.
Oh, Lord knows I need that spell for many guys.
But just then, Ashley came to our table.
She was the school's biggest and meanest bully.
She had been away for a month visiting her relatives in Sweden, and apparently, peace ended the second she came back.
Well, well, well.
I leave for 1 month, and suddenly you think you run this place?
This is my table. Move.
Excuse me? I wasn't talking to you, wannabe.
Ugly makeover, by the way.
What's wrong, V?
Cat got your tongue?
But Mom just stared at her without saying a word, which was very weird.
Are you deaf or something?
I don't usually talk back, but Mom looked so frozen that I felt like I had to say something.
No, she just can't remember hearing about you.
I guess your reputation wasn't as life-changing as you thought.
Ashley scoffed and shoved me.
I shoved her back.
And a few kids quickly stepped in and pulled her away while she kept cursing and threatening us.
Mom didn't even try to protect me.
I turned to her and gave her a look like, "Seriously?" What?
I let you handle it.
I'm not getting involved in teen drama.
Now, let's go to class.
But something about that felt very weird, because my mom never backed away from drama.
Days passed, and Grandma's health wasn't getting any better.
To make it worse, she didn't remember the exact date Mom had to be ready for the transformation.
It's somewhere between December and February.
Great. Very specific.
And I still hadn't gotten Miles to like me.
By the way, he had stopped talking to Mom, but he was still obsessed with his notebook.
And even though he had short-term memory issues, he was really smart, especially in chemistry.
One day in chemistry class, I was assigned to work with Miles.
I tried to act nonchalant because if he wasn't going to notice me, then I wasn't going to notice him either.
You're holding the beakers so steady.
It's like you were born for this.
Oh, wow. Thank you.
Aren't you the sweetest?
Then he pulled out his notebook and scribbled something down.
What? Did you write that I have magical beaker hands?
But when I glanced at his notebook, I saw the letter V written all over the page.
Okay, seriously, what do you want from V?
Why are you so obsessed with her? Obsessed? Me?
No, I just need to tell her something, but she won't listen to me.
He looked around, then lowered his voice.
Something's wrong with her eyes.
Most people wouldn't notice it, but the whites of her eyes aren't fully white.
There's this faint silver shade around the edges.
At first, I thought it was the lighting, but I saw it three times.
He flipped the notebook toward me.
It said, "Silver in eyes.
Getting stronger. Not normal.
Tell her." Also, not to be mean, but doesn't she look a little older than 16?
Maybe she got held back a couple of years or three.
Poor thing. Yeah, definitely.
She's just so dumb.
I looked at Mom, and she flashed me a smile, then gestured for me to keep talking to Miles.
But her face immediately dropped when Ashley walked up to her.
Ashley suddenly shoved the beakers and test tubes off the table, and they shattered so loudly that the whole class froze.
Did you tell people that I was a dumb, useless, good-for-nothing witch?
Uh, not not in that particular order.
Ashley gasped, her eyes widening, then grabbed Mom by the collar.
That was when I rushed over and pushed her away.
What is your problem, dude?
Stay out of it, weirdo. Or what?
I got so close to her that our foreheads touched and we were both breathing like angry bulls.
Then the teacher came and pulled us apart.
While Ashley was still glaring at me like she wanted me dead, I turned around, but Mom wasn't there.
I felt overwhelmed, so I went to the bathroom to wash my face.
I was standing by the sink, writing my initials and Miles' on the mirror, when I heard a faint crying sound.
I got closer and tried to open the stall door.
Surprisingly, it was unlocked.
And even more surprisingly, Mom was sitting there, crying like a little baby. Ma?
Nothing. It's just onions. What onions?
We're in a school bathroom.
Also, you haven't touched a stove since I was five.
Ma, are you okay?
I I just don't know how to stand up to bullies. What? You?
You're the strongest, craziest woman I know.
Not when I was 16.
Back then I was insecure and weak.
There were rumors that I came from a family of witches and I became an easy target.
I didn't know how to defend myself.
The day I was supposed to transform, I wasn't partying like Grandma thinks.
I was here, in a bathroom, crying because a bully had humiliated me.
Mom told me that after high school, she and Grandma moved to another town…
and her way of dealing with her failure was making jokes, going out with guys,
and pretending nothing hurt her.
But deep down, she knew she had disappointed Grandma.
I didn't know Mom had been holding all that inside.
So I walked over and hugged her tight.
It's okay, Ma.
We can fix this together.
Mom suddenly covered her mouth.
Oh, honey, did you eat falafel?
Mom, I'm literally trying to comfort you.
Mom gently pushed my face away.
That was beautiful.
Now, say it facing the wall.
For the next few weeks, Mom and I stuck together.
But then I noticed the silver line around the edges of her eyes were getting bigger.
So I suggested she wear sunglasses.
A few days later, her hair started turning gray, too.
No matter how many times she dyed it, the gray kept coming back.
So she started wearing hats every day.
But that will make Ashley pick on me even more.
And that was exactly what happened.
Ashley had even more minions join her, and they all laughed at Mom.
Whenever I defended her, they laughed even harder.
Aw, look at that.
So we Butterman is protecting this loser, Shady V and her body fart.
When Ashley walked away, Mom looked completely defeated.
I'm going to hide in the bathroom until I die.
But you'll miss your transformation.
Then Mom pulled me closer and put her hands on my shoulders.
Then help me.
So I tried talking to Miles.
Maybe he could help with all the chemistry mumbo jumbo.
Hey, so remember that faint silver line you noticed around V's eyes?
Do you know any chemistry magic that could make it disappear? Yeah, sure.
Let me just grab the silver eye reversal potion I use every Tuesday.
Oh, please hurry.
I need it before Tuesday.
We both laughed, and then I found myself asking him something.
Do you believe in witches?
Well, I have no reason not to.
Science explains a lot of things, but not everything.
I don't know why, but that made me feel closer to him.
Most people would have called me crazy, but Miles just accepted it like I had asked him to believe in Canada.
Then Miles offered me some Fanta, and I drank it in one go.
I was so thirsty.
Congrats, you just drank a love potion.
Now you love me.
Uh no, I don't think it's working.
By the way, I liked your hair and style before you copied that V girl.
I don't want to be mean, but how do you even remember how I looked?
I have short-term memory problems, not blindness.
Then he showed me a sketch in his notebook, and it was of me.
Please don't think I'm some obsessive weirdo.
I just draw things I like.
We both laughed again, and somehow we ended up exchanging numbers.
Days turned into weeks, and I started getting closer to Miles.
I even helped him with his memory, but Mom still needed my help all the time.
Cuz I couldn't just stand there and let Ashley and her minions bully her.
I'm sorry, honey.
I'm ruining your best years.
Oh, Mom, don't say that.
If you think about it, you kind of made my life better.
I never had a reason to be strong or defend anyone before, but now look at me, getting into fights and stuff.
The Zoe from a few months ago would never believe this.
I kept talking, but Mom suddenly noticed someone walking down the hallway.
He was a nice-looking man in his 40s, so Mom gently shoved me aside.
Later. Later.
Hey, you. Are you lost, sir?
Yeah, actually, I'm Miles's dad.
He forgot his notebook, and I really need to give it to him. Oh, Miles?
I'll walk miles to help you find Miles.
I do Miles' yards and feet, and eyes, and hair.
With that, Ashley walked by and snatched Mom's hat off while one of her minions yanked off her sunglasses.
Mom's eyes were even more silver now, and everyone gasped.
Jeez, somebody call 911.
Are you okay, kid?
But the kids started laughing and pointing at Mom while she sank to the floor hugging her knees with terrified silver eyes and wild gray hair.
I couldn't just stand there and watch her like that.
So, I lunged at Ashley, but she fought back and shoved me against the lockers.
Then, she pulled the hair stick out of her bun and came at me with it.
I was too frozen to move.
I just closed my eyes.
Then, I heard Mom scream, "Stay away from her."
When I opened my eyes, Ashley had already slashed Mom's arm, but Mom didn't care.
She looked like a lioness protecting her cub.
She broke the hair stick in half,
grabbed Ashley's arm and twisted it behind her back.
You stay away from my baby.
Nobody touches my baby.
Everyone stared, terrified.
Then, Mom shoved Ashley away, and Ashley stumbled back with pure fear on her face.
Anyone else want to try me? Come on.
I'm not scared of you anymore.
Come at me if you dare, you useless, brainless bullies.
Most of the kids ran.
A few teachers tried to calm Mom down, but she was too fired up.
She pushed past them and came straight to me, pulling me into the tightest hug.
Mom was a petite woman, but in that moment, her hug felt like the biggest, warmest shield in the world.
Then, my phone buzzed.
It was a message from Grandma.
Grandma says she remembers the transformation date.
Mom, it was 30 minutes ago.
You missed it.
Funny, the first time I missed it because I was hiding from a bully.
This time I missed it because I finally stood up to one.
Come on, baby.
Let's go home.
When we got home, Grandma was in the kitchen cooking dinner like nothing had happened.
Mom and I froze. What?
I was sick, not dead.
Stop staring at me like I came back from the grave.
I had some complications, but I'm only 72.
Mom turned to me, triumphant.
I knew it.
Told you she wasn't 67.
Mom, really? Grandma, you said Mom had to become a witch to save you.
And look at her.
She finally stood up for herself.
So, yes, I'd say she transformed.
Wait, so I'm a witch now?
Grandma stared at her for a second, then burst out laughing. A witch? Please.
The only thing you ever enchanted was stupid men.
So, none of it was real? The magic?
No. The problem? Very real.
After the bullying in high school, your mother never really recovered.
That girl humiliated her so badly that Vicky stopped believing she could face anything hard.
So, she hid behind jokes, flirting, and pretending nothing mattered before anyone could hurt her first.
Deep down, she was still that scared 16-year-old girl hiding in the bathroom.
I tried everything to make her face herself, and I was almost out of hope.
Then I found those medical test results she never bothered to open.
Medical results? Yes.
You have a rare pigment condition.
That's what caused the silver in your eyes and the gray in your hair. Not magic.
Not a curse.
Just your body being dramatic, which honestly fits you.
So, you used it to make us believe she was turning into a witch?
I used what I had, and it worked.
She went back as that scared 16-year-old girl, but this time, she didn't run.
She faced the thing that broke her and protected her daughter.
That's more powerful than any spell.
Mom frowned like she wanted to argue, but then she looked at me, and I was smiling, and we both immediately started laughing.
Well, I guess I should go then.
It was a pleasure being your bestie, daughter.
You'll always be my bestie, Mom.
I didn't even know I could be brave until I had to protect you.
Okay, off I go.
Also, I heard Ashley's dad is rich and newly divorced.
Maybe I can become her stepmom. Oh, god.
